definitions.explanation: An official position in government or public service. Includes elected officials, civil servants, and other positions of public trust.

examples.japanese: {汚職|おしょく}で{公職|こうしょく}を{追|お}われた。
examples.english: They were removed from public office due to corruption.

examples.japanese: {公職|こうしょく}{選挙法|せんきょほう}では{選挙|せんきょ}{運動|うんどう}のルールが{細|こま}かく{定|さだ}められている。
examples.english: The Public Offices Election Act sets out detailed rules for campaign activities.

notes: Composed of {公|こう} (public) + {職|しょく} (position, office). A formal term used in legal and political contexts. Common collocations: {公職|こうしょく}に{就|つ}く (to assume public office), {公職|こうしょく}を{辞|じ}する (to resign from public office), {公職|こうしょく}{選挙|せんきょ} (public office election), {公職|こうしょく}{追放|ついほう} (purge from public office). The {公職|こうしょく}{選挙法|せんきょほう} (Public Offices Election Act) is a key Japanese law governing all aspects of elections. After WWII, the {公職|こうしょく}{追放|ついほう} (public office purge) barred wartime leaders from government positions.
